# Introduction

This is a fixture document. It is used to confirm that a deployment of the
compilation service can render a manuscript end to end, and to give anyone
writing a client something to submit that does not depend on a private
repository.

Nothing here is a finding. The subject, sorting small coloured blocks, was
chosen because it is obviously not research, so no sentence in this document can
be mistaken for a claim about the world [@example2020placeholder].

## What this document exercises

Prior fixtures have failed to catch real defects because they were too simple: a
single paragraph renders under almost any misconfiguration. This one includes
each construct that has actually broken a build.

- A figure with a caption and a cross-reference, since a figure referenced by a
  path that does not resolve stops the render.
- A table with a caption and a label, since captions separated from their table
  are a common defect.
- Several citations, since a bibliography that is not sent is reported only as a
  warning and the citations then silently vanish [@sample2019method;
  @demo2021analysis].
- Inline code such as `sort_blocks()` and a fenced block, since raw blocks and
  code spans take different paths through the renderer.

# Method

Blocks were placed on a table and sorted by colour. The procedure was repeated
three times. No blocks were harmed.

```python
def sort_blocks(blocks):
    """Sort by colour. This is a fixture, not an implementation."""
    return sorted(blocks, key=lambda b: b.colour)
```

The approach follows no established protocol, because there is none
[@sample2019method].

The counts sum to nine, which is the only verifiable statement in this document.

# Discussion

If this document rendered, the deployment can parse a manuscript, resolve a
figure path, number and reference a figure and a table, resolve citations
against a bibliography, and produce the requested output formats.

If it did not, the failure is in the deployment rather than the document, which
is the point of having a fixture [@demo2021analysis].
